results.text:
**Sideboard for your Dimir Tempo list (Legacy)**

Your main deck is card-for-card the 5-0 Legacy League list from the archetype data, so I left all 60 untouched and built only the 15.

**Sideboard (15)**
- 3 Consign to Memory
- 2 Force of Negation
- 2 Barrowgoyf
- 2 Hydroblast
- 2 Bloodchief's Thirst
- 2 Surgical Extraction
- 1 Massacre
- 1 Nihil Spellbomb

**Plan:** The main deck stays a cheap-threat tempo deck backed by Daze, Force of Will and Wasteland. The board gives you narrow answers to the decks that beat that plan. All of it is cheap or free, so it fits a deck that wants to keep mana for counterspells.

**Why these cards:**
- **Consign to Memory (3):** It counters triggered abilities or colorless spells. The tool shows it mostly in OmniTell, Blink and Sneak and Show lists. In the meta data, Tron is 7.1%, Eldrazi Aggro 6.1%, OmniTell 4.4%, Blink 3.8% and Sneak and Show 2.5%. It also answers Ocelot Aggro's triggers. Nearly every Dimir list (98.2%) runs it in the board.
- **Force of Negation (2):** It counters noncreature spells for free on the opponent's turn. It is aimed at Doomsday (5.8%), Tron, Izzet Tempo, Storm, Beanstalk and Blink. The tool shows it popular in Doomsday, Tron, Izzet and Blink lists.
- **Hydroblast (2):** Ocelot Aggro is the second-biggest deck at 9%, and its sideboards play Pyroblast (84.6%). Its red cards include Amped Raptor and Goblin Bombardment. Hydroblast also hits Izzet Tempo (4.6%). The reference list ran 1; I went to 2 because those two decks add up to roughly 13.6% of the field.
- **Bloodchief's Thirst (2):** It kills Ocelot Pride, Guide of Souls, Ajani (a mana-value-2 planeswalker) and Death and Taxes creatures. Kicked, it kills a bigger creature or planeswalker late. It supplements your 4 Fatal Push.
- **Barrowgoyf (2):** It has deathtouch and lifelink, so it holds off aggro like Ocelot, Eldrazi and Death and Taxes and wins grindy games against GX Midrange. The reference list ran 3. I cut one so the slots could go to the graveyard cards.
- **Massacre (1):** It is free when the opponent controls a Plains and you control a Swamp. Ocelot Aggro and Death and Taxes play Plains, so it can sweep their small creatures. It also shrinks your own Bowmasters and Tamiyo, so I kept it to 1.
- **Surgical Extraction (2) and Nihil Spellbomb (1):** These are the graveyard hate for Reanimator (3.8%), Sewer Combo (3.4%) and Hogaak (2%). Surgical costs no mana, which suits your tempo plan. Spellbomb replaces itself. I skipped Leyline of the Void, which the reference list ran as 4. It is dead if you draw it late, and I judged one fewer dead slot against the 9.2% of graveyard decks was the better deal.

**Sideboarding:**
- **Ocelot Aggro, Death and Taxes:** Bring in Massacre, Bloodchief's Thirst, Hydroblast (Ocelot only) and Barrowgoyf. Take out Daze and Thoughtseize, whose value drops against cheap creatures.
- **Tron, Eldrazi Aggro:** Bring in Consign to Memory. Add Force of Negation against Tron. Take out Fatal Push and Bloodchief's Thirst-type removal.
- **Doomsday, Storm, Beanstalk, OmniTell, Sneak and Show, Blink:** Bring in Force of Negation and Consign to Memory. Take out the slow or situational creature removal.
- **Izzet Tempo:** Bring in Hydroblast, plus Consign to Memory if they run colorless or trigger-based cards.
- **Reanimator, Sewer Combo, Hogaak:** Bring in Surgical Extraction and Nihil Spellbomb. Take out cards that do little against them, such as Wasteland-heavy draws.
- **GX Midrange:** Bring in Barrowgoyf and Bloodchief's Thirst.

**Mana (measured on the main deck):** In 5,000 simulated games the mulligan rate was 8.7%. Colored mana was available in 86.5% of games by turn 2 and 87.6% by turn 3. Screw rate was 29.2%, and average lands in play were 2.5 by turn 3. This matches the reference list exactly, because the main deck is the same. check_deck reports 19 lands, against an archetype mean of 18.94, and the tool recommends about 20. I left that alone since you asked for a sideboard only.

**Label:** Tuned. The main deck is the stock 5-0 list. The sideboard borrows the Dimir archetype's most common cards, adjusted to the meta shares above.

**Unverified:** I did not check the Sewer Combo and Hogaak lists directly. Treating them as graveyard-reliant decks is my judgment from their names and the tool listing Surgical Extraction and Spellbomb in Hogaak lists.

results.prompt: Combine Living End and Scam into one Modern deck.
results.text:
**Verdict:** I resubmitted the deck with two changes, and it was accepted as a brew. Its worst matchups are Broodscale and Prowess. Its worst weakness is mana.

**Plan.** "Scam" isn't a card in the pool. I read it as the evoke-Elemental shell: Deceit, Shriekmaw, Subtlety and Endurance. Cascade (Shardless Agent, Violent Outburst, Demonic Dread) puts Living End on the stack. Living End has mana value 0, so it is the only card those cascades can hit. The evoke Elementals and Street Wraith fill the graveyard with big creatures first, and Shriekmaw's removal trigger fires again when it returns. Subtlety and Endurance protect the turn.

**Changes from the submitted list.**
- **Force of Negation:** I added 1 to the main deck, replacing the second Oliphaunt. Force of Negation is a counterspell for noncreature spells. It is the best answer to Broodscale's noncreature spells. The tools show Broodscale (14.4% of the field) running Kozilek's Command and Malevolent Rumble. Force of Negation also appears in 100% of the Living End lists the tool returned, usually as 4 copies.
- **Sideboard:** it already held 3 Force of Negation. I moved 1 into the main deck and the other 2 stay as sideboard cards, since a counterspell is dead against creature-heavy decks.
- **Wistfulness:** I wanted 2 in the main deck, but the main deck can't go above 60% overlap with an existing Living End list. Wistfulness is 100% of those lists, so I dropped it.
- **Curator of Mysteries:** I wanted to cut it to 1, but the locked engine needs 2.

**Mana.** The tools returned these numbers for the final 16-land list with 4 Street Wraith:
- The simulation (5,000 games) gives an 11.1% mulligan rate and 42% screw. The lands drop to 2.72 in play by turn 4.
- Color access is the soft spot. I measured 79% on turn 3 for the revised 16-land version, against 86.8% for a real Living End list.
- I did not simulate the final submitted list, only the 16-land revised variant. The final list should be about the same, but that is judgment.
- The cause is Demonic Dread (needs B and R), because it makes the deck four-colour. I can't fix that without changing the locked engine.
- A 17th land made colors worse (74.7% on turn 3). A basic Island doesn't help the three coloured cascade spells.
- Blue sources are only 8, against about 10.4 in real lists. Treat this as the main risk.
- The simulator measures land drops and colors only. The "engine ready by turn 3" figure was 14.2%. Cascade creatures in hand by turn 3 was 40.4%.

**Matchups, from the meta data.**
- **Broodscale (14.4%):** a hard matchup. Their turn-3-or-4 plan is mostly noncreature spells, so Force of Negation and Mystical Dispute help. Subtlety can hit Emrakul, but I didn't verify that interaction.
- **Prowess (9.9%):** also hard. Lightning Bolt and Lava Dart kill our cascade creature, and they board Tormod's Crypt and Surgical Extraction (47% and 48.6% of Prowess lists). Living End does sweep their creatures. Hold Endurance and Subtlety as blockers.
- **Others:** Energy, Blink and Affinity are untested. I'd expect Affinity to be better after boarding Foundation Breaker, Force of Vigor and Damping Sphere (judgment, not measured).

**Sideboarding.**
- **Against Broodscale and Goryo's Vengeance:** bring in Force of Negation, Mystical Dispute, and Inevitable Betrayal if they keep creatures in the deck.
- **Against Affinity:** bring in Force of Vigor, Foundation Breaker and Damping Sphere. Damping Sphere also helps against Storm.
- **Against Prowess:** bring in Dismember for their early creatures. Keep Endurance in the deck to turn off their graveyard plan. Cut Curator of Mysteries and Troll of Khazad-dûm, which are too slow.
- **Against graveyard hate and counterspells:** keep Subtlety and the Force of Negation copies, and cut the clunky big creatures.

**Label.** This is a brew. It borrows the Living End shell: 4 each of Endurance, Subtlety, Shardless Agent, Violent Outburst and Street Wraith, plus the usual dual lands and fetches.

**Unverified.** I have not measured win rates against any matchup. The matchup assessments are judgment based on the meta data.

intent.goal: Build a Modern deck that merges Living End's cascade-into-Living End reanimation plan with Scam's Grief/Undying Evil-style discard and evoke shell into a coherent list.

engine.thesis: "Scam" isn't a card, and the tools show its core pieces Grief and Fury are banned in Modern, so I read it as the evoke-Elemental discard/disruption shell. Evoking Deceit and Shriekmaw gives cheap interaction and fills the graveyard with big creatures for Living End, and Shriekmaw's removal trigger fires again on the way back. Modern fits because Living End is legal and Subtlety and Endurance are already in its lists.
engine.winCondition: Cascade into Living End on turn 3 (or suspend it) with 3+ creatures in the graveyard, wiping the opponent's board while mine returns and Shriekmaw kills a creature. The recurred creatures then beat down while Subtlety and Endurance protect the turn.
beats: Slower creature/midrange decks that can't punish a turn-3 sweep-and-reanimate
Combo decks, via Subtlety and Deceit disruption
Creature-light control decks, since Living End then only returns my side
losesTo: Graveyard hate such as Endurance-style effects, Cling to Dust and Leyline of the Void
Fast aggro like Prowess, Broodscale and Energy that race the setup turns
Counterspells on the cascade spell, and removal on the cascade creature in response
Undying Evil and Not Dead After All are cut because 1-mana cards would be blank cascade hits

results.prompt: Build a Commander deck with Atraxa, Praetors' Voice that's all about proliferate.
results.text:
**Atraxa, Praetors' Voice proliferate deck, revised once (brew, borrowing the proliferate/counters shell)**

**Plan.** Land Atraxa on turn 4, or turn 3 with ramp. Atraxa proliferates every end step, and cheap proliferate spells and doublers grow +1/+1 counters, loyalty and poison. Atraxa and the other counter-laden creatures win in combat as a flying, lifelinking body. Planeswalker ultimates (Ajani, Sleeper Agent's poison emblem; Vraska's -9) are the backup finish.

**What I changed in review.** There is no meta data for Commander, so I judged the matchups from the card pool and the locked list's own weaknesses.
- **The weak points.** The deck's worst matchups are fast combo, wraths and mass bounce, and stax or counter-hate. The original had plenty of removal but no way to stop a combo piece or a wrath on the stack. It also ran 36 lands plus about 10 ramp spells, a lot of mana for an average mana value of 3.
- **The swap.** I cut one Forest and one Island, the two colours with spare sources (G and U were at 19.5). I added Fierce Guardianship and Force of Will. Both are free to cast (Guardianship while you control Atraxa; Force by pitching a blue card), so you can hold up protection while still developing.
- **What I left alone.** The engine and the colour balance of the fixing are unchanged.

**Key cards**
- **Repeatable proliferate:** Atraxa herself, Evolution Sage, Thrummingbird, Flux Channeler, Tekuthal, Contagion Engine, Contagion Clasp, Karn's Bastion, Tromell and Ichormoon Gauntlet.
- **Doublers:** Doubling Season, Hardened Scales, Winding Constrictor, Corpsejack Menace, Branching Evolution, Pir and Vorinclex.
- **Planeswalkers:** Ajani, Sleeper Agent, Ajani Steadfast, Ajani, the Greathearted, Archangel Elspeth, Oko and The Wandering Emperor. Proliferate adds loyalty every turn.
- **Cantrips that proliferate:** Contentious Plan, Experimental Augury, Tezzeret's Gambit, Atomize and Mutational Advantage.
- **Protection:** Teferi's Protection, Heroic Intervention, Swiftfoot Boots and the new counterspells.
- **Interaction:** Swords to Plowshares, Path to Exile, Vindicate, Anguished Unmaking, Beast Within and Cyclonic Rift.

**Mana.** The deck has 34 lands and about 10 ramp or mana-rock cards. Colour sources are W 17.5, U 19.5, B 17.5 and G 19.5, measured before the Forest/Island cut; the cut only touched G and U.
- The check tool still suggests about 38 lands for this curve, and warns that W and B sit at 17.5 sources where Elspeth and Yawgmoth want about 27. That is a real limit of a four-colour deck, and the ramp that fetches basics partly makes up for it. If you find you stumble on lands, put the Forest and Island back.
- The simulation had some flaws. Atraxa was in the library rather than the command zone, so the numbers are slightly pessimistic. Its figures were:
  - mulligan rate 9.2%
  - all four colours available by turn 4 in about 78% of games
  - a proliferate engine piece cast by turn 4 in 33.8% of games
- The land-drop and "screw" figures (46.3% of games with all four land drops by turn 4) are an opening-turns model only. It ignores ramp, fetches and cantrips, so don't read them as the deck's real mana.

**Adjusting for matchups.** Commander has no sideboard, so these are swaps for the 99 between games.
- **Fast combo:** keep Force of Will and Fierce Guardianship, and hold Cyclonic Rift for the combo turn. Cut Sword of Truth and Justice or Norn's Choirmaster for a cheap counterspell like Counterspell or Mana Drain. Both are legal, though I haven't tested them.
- **Wrath or bounce decks:** don't overextend. Keep Teferi's Protection and Heroic Intervention up, lean on planeswalkers, and consider adding Eternal Witness. I checked that it is legal but haven't tested it here.
- **Counter-hate such as Solemnity, or opposing Vorinclex halving:** use Beast Within, Vindicate and Anguished Unmaking on it. Cankerbloom and Boseiju also kill enchantments or artifacts.
- **Slow creature decks:** these are the best matchups. A lifelinking flier plus Swords or Path keeps you ahead.

**Unverified.** Nothing here is tested against real opposing decks, and no Commander tournament data was available. The matchup claims are judgment. The land count is below the tool's recommendation, as noted above.

engine.thesis: Atraxa, Praetors' Voice proliferates every end step, and a package of cheap repeatable proliferate effects, counter doublers and planeswalkers turns that into growing +1/+1 counters, loyalty and poison. Four-colour Commander is the right home because Atraxa needs all of G/W/U/B and those colours hold nearly every proliferate and counter card.
engine.winCondition: Grow a flying, lifelinking Atraxa and other counter-laden creatures until they win in combat. Planeswalker ultimates (Ajani, Sleeper Agent's poison emblem; Vraska's -9) and poison counters from Contagion Engine are backup finishers.

Control and stax decks that don't remove a planeswalker or Atraxa quickly
Table-wide pods where life gain and counters outgrow opposing boards
losesTo: Fast combo that wins before turn 5
Repeated removal or counterspells on Atraxa (the end-step trigger is the core engine)
Wrath effects and mass bounce that reset counters
Counter-hate such as Solemnity or opposing Vorinclex halving
